A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 31-page versions of the same work. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-I without material gaps.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original synthetic simulations and vision-model attack experiments. Appendix H adds OME and NLP experiments, including Tables 4-6 and ROC results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations and vision/NLP attack experiments in Section 5 and Appendix H, including their reported outcomes.

M1.justification: The FC-based and attention-based attack procedures, including the ViT adaptation, are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices C and G.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic, vision, and NLP coverage, including one-hot and spherical data, CIFAR10/CIFAR100/ImageNet, and IMDB/Yelp/Twitter/Finance evaluations.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison sets are identical. Tables 4-6 retain the same FC-based and attention-based attack rows under GRR, RAPPOR, and dBitFlipPM; main-text and OME comparisons also retain their participants.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain identical model configurations, preprocessing, batch dimensions, privacy budgets, hyperparameter settings, and evaluation metrics. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The batch-size analysis in Figure 9, beta sensitivity analysis in Figure 10, synthetic noise/dimension analyses, and Appendix H.3 ROC analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix G and Table 1 retain the same simulation and trial/game counts, including 20 trials of 200 games for several experiments. Statistical and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Experimental curves, numerical table entries, rankings, and qualitative findings are identical, including Tables 4-6 and Figure 16. No empirical result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 in Section 4.1 and its restatement in Appendix D.1 replace '=' with '≥' for the FC adversary's advantage. This changes an exact equality to a lower bound, matching the unchanged proof's Equation (20). Assumptions and derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion are unchanged. They already describe lower-bound guarantees and persistent privacy risks under LDP; the theorem correction does not revise these headline claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the privacy-utility trade-off, attention behavior, limitations of applying the continuous-domain theory to NLP, and secure-aggregation qualifications in Appendix I are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains identical software/hardware information, embedding and preprocessing instructions, hyperparameter-selection procedures, and LDP implementation details. No reproducibility or code/data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and Appendix I retain the same cited works and positioning relative to prior inference attacks and alternative privacy protections.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 16 June 2025 to v2 dated 1 August 2025. Prose, terminology, authorship, and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-16 and Tables 1-6 retain identical displays, captions, and placement. Algorithms and page layout are also unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves a localized theorem/proof inconsistency: Theorem 1 and its appendix restatement now state the lower bound actually derived in Equation (20), rather than an unsupported exact equality. This improves mathematical accuracy while leaving the methods, empirical evidence, and broader conclusions unchanged.
